title: Jai alai, the fastest ball
hook: A jai alai ball once hit 302 km/h, flung from a wicker basket at a stone wall.
peek: In jai alai, players catch and hurl a hard ball with a long curved basket strapped to one arm. Guinness long listed one throw at 302 km/h as the fastest ball speed in sport, though golf has since challenged it.
lede: Jai alai is a Basque form of pelota. Players wear a cesta, a long curved wicker basket, and use it to catch a rock-hard ball and sling it against the front wall of a three-walled court called a fronton. In 1979 José Ramón Areitio was clocked at 302 km/h in Newport, Rhode Island, a figure Guinness recorded as the fastest ball speed in any sport.

bullets.text: The basket is made from reeds woven over a chestnut frame and is shaped to the player's hand. Catching and throwing happen in one smooth sweep, which turns the long arm and basket into a sling.
The ball is a little smaller than a baseball, with a core of rubber wound tight and covered in goatskin. It is harder than a golf ball, which is why modern players wear helmets.
The fastest-ball title is now doubtful. Long-drive golfers have been measured launching balls even faster, so jai alai's record is best described as one of the fastest.
Basque players brought the game to the Americas, and in the 20th century it became a betting sport in Florida, where frontons once drew big crowds. Few remain today.
